title: OSHA general industry occupational noise exposure practice questions
description: Free OSHA noise practice questions on 29 CFR 1910.95: Table G-16, the 85 dB action level, audiograms and hearing protectors, each linked to its source.

questions.question: Under 1910.95(b)(2), when are variations in noise level to be considered continuous?

options.A: When they involve maxima at intervals of 1 second or less
options.B: When they involve maxima at intervals of 10 seconds or more
options.C: When the level never drops below 85 dBA
options.D: Only when they are measured with a dosimeter

questions.explanation: "If the variations in noise level involve maxima at intervals of 1 second or less, it is to be considered continuous."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A day's noise exposure is made up of periods at different levels. Under the footnote to Table G-16, when should the mixed exposure be considered to exceed the limit value?

options.A: When any single period exceeds 85 dBA
options.B: When the plain average of the levels exceeds 90 dBA
options.C: When the sum of the fractions C1/T1 + C2/T2 ... Cn/Tn exceeds unity
options.D: When there are more than three separate periods

questions.explanation: When exposure has two or more periods of different levels, "their combined effect should be considered, rather than the individual effect of each." If the sum of the fractions exceeds unity, "the mixed exposure should be considered to exceed the limit value."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.95(a), how are sound levels measured when they are compared with Table G-16?

options.A: On the C scale of a sound level meter at fast response
options.B: On the A scale of a standard sound level meter at slow response
options.C: On the A scale at impulse response
options.D: In peak decibels with no weighting

questions.explanation: Protection is required when sound levels exceed Table G-16 "when measured on the A scale of a standard sound level meter at slow response."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What opportunity does 1910.95(f) require the employer to give affected employees or their representatives?

options.A: To choose the monitoring contractor
options.B: To set the action level for their own department
options.C: To skip audiometric testing
options.D: To observe any noise measurements conducted under the section

questions.explanation: "The employer shall provide affected employees or their representatives with an opportunity to observe any noise measurements conducted pursuant to this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When employee noise exposures are computed for the hearing conservation program, how is the attenuation of hearing protectors treated?

options.A: The full NRR is subtracted from the measured level
options.B: It is not counted: exposures are computed without regard to it
options.C: Half of the NRR is subtracted from the measured level
options.D: 7 dB is subtracted from the measured level

questions.explanation: For the hearing conservation program, exposures are computed under Appendix A and Table G-16a "without regard to any attenuation provided by the use of personal protective equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Paragraphs (c) through (n) of 1910.95 do not apply to employers engaged in which operations?

options.A: Oil and gas well drilling and servicing operations
options.B: Food processing operations
options.C: Printing operations
options.D: Sawmill operations

questions.explanation: Paragraphs (c) through (n) "shall not apply to employers engaged in oil and gas well drilling and servicing operations."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A new machine raises noise so that additional employees may be exposed at or above the action level. What does 1910.95(d)(3) require?

options.A: Nothing until the next annual audiogram
options.B: Only a warning sign at the machine
options.C: Only a written notice to OSHA
options.D: Monitoring shall be repeated

questions.explanation: "Monitoring shall be repeated whenever a change in production, process, equipment or controls increases noise exposures to the extent that" additional employees may be exposed at or above the action level, or hearing protector attenuation may become inadequate.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: High worker mobility makes area monitoring generally inappropriate at a plant. What must the employer use for monitoring, unless it can show area sampling produces equivalent results?

options.A: A single area reading taken once a year
options.B: Readings taken only at the loudest machine
options.C: Representative personal sampling
options.D: Employee answers to a noise questionnaire

questions.explanation: Where high worker mobility, significant variations in sound level, or a significant component of impulse noise make area monitoring generally inappropriate, the employer "shall use representative personal sampling" unless it can show that area sampling produces equivalent results.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which appendix to 1910.95 is labeled non-mandatory?

options.A: Appendix A, Noise Exposure Computation
options.B: Appendix B, Methods for Estimating the Adequacy of Hearing Protector Attenuation
options.C: Appendix F, Calculations and Application of Age Corrections to Audiograms
options.D: Appendix D, Audiometric Test Rooms

questions.explanation: Appendix F's heading says "This appendix Is Non-Mandatory." Paragraph (n)(1) states that Appendices A, B, C, D and E "are mandatory."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Appendix F (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.95(g)(3), which technician does not need to be certified to perform audiometric tests?

options.A: A technician who operates microprocessor audiometers
options.B: A technician who tests fewer than 50 employees a year
options.C: Any technician supervised by the plant manager
options.D: A technician with five years of experience

questions.explanation: "A technician who operates microprocessor audiometers does not need to be certified." A technician who performs audiometric tests must still be responsible to an audiologist, otolaryngologist or physician.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where mobile test vans are used to meet the audiometric testing obligation, the valid baseline audiogram must be obtained within what time of first exposure at or above the action level?

options.A: Within 2 years
options.B: Within 1 year
options.C: Within 3 years
options.D: Within 5 years

questions.explanation: Under the mobile test van exception, the employer "shall obtain a valid baseline audiogram within 1 year of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee's annual audiogram shows a standard threshold shift. What does 1910.95(g)(7)(ii) allow the employer to do?

options.A: Discard the annual audiogram and wait a year
options.B: Replace the baseline audiogram with it, with no professional review
options.C: Postpone any retest until the next annual audiogram
options.D: Obtain a retest within 30 days and consider the results of the retest as the annual audiogram

questions.explanation: "If the annual audiogram shows that an employee has suffered a standard threshold shift, the employer may obtain a retest within 30 days and consider the results of the retest as the annual audiogram."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.95(g)(2) say about what the audiometric testing program costs employees?

options.A: It is provided at no cost to employees
options.B: Employees pay half of each test
options.C: Employees pay for annual audiograms only
options.D: Employees pay for the baseline audiogram only

questions.explanation: "The program shall be provided at no cost to employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In determining whether a standard threshold shift has occurred, what allowance does 1910.95(g)(10)(ii) permit?

options.A: Subtracting the hearing protector's noise reduction rating
options.B: Ignoring any ear the employee says was exposed to loud music
options.C: Averaging the result with a coworker's audiogram
options.D: Allowance for the contribution of aging (presbycusis), by correcting the annual audiogram according to Appendix F

questions.explanation: "allowance may be made for the contribution of aging (presbycusis) to the change in hearing level by correcting the annual audiogram according to the procedure described in appendix F".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Later testing of an employee exposed to less than an 8-hour TWA of 90 decibels shows that a standard threshold shift is not persistent. What does 1910.95(g)(8)(iii) allow?

options.A: Disregarding the shift without telling the employee
options.B: Discontinuing the required use of hearing protectors for that employee, after informing the employee of the new interpretation
options.C: Deleting the employee's earlier audiometric records
options.D: Removing the employee from the training program

questions.explanation: In that case the employer "Shall inform the employee of the new audiometric interpretation" and "May discontinue the required use of hearing protectors for that employee."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee who does not use hearing protectors has a standard threshold shift, and no physician has found it is not work related. What must the employer ensure?

options.A: The employee is moved out of the noisy job permanently
options.B: The employee receives a written warning
options.C: The employee is fitted with hearing protectors, trained in their use and care, and required to use them
options.D: The employee is retested every month until hearing returns

questions.explanation: Unless a physician determines the shift is not work related or aggravated by occupational noise, "Employees not using hearing protectors shall be fitted with hearing protectors, trained in their use and care, and required to use them."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee exposed to an 8-hour TWA of 87 decibels has experienced a standard threshold shift. What does 1910.95(i)(2) require?

options.A: Hearing protectors are optional for this employee
options.B: Hearing protectors are required only above an 8-hour TWA of 90 decibels
options.C: Hearing protectors are required only if the employee asks for them
options.D: The employer must ensure hearing protectors are worn

questions.explanation: Employers must ensure hearing protectors are worn by any employee "exposed to an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels or greater" who has experienced a standard threshold shift.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 1910.95(i)(3) involve employees in choosing hearing protectors?

options.A: They are given the opportunity to select their hearing protectors from a variety of suitable hearing protectors provided by the employer
options.B: They must buy their own hearing protectors
options.C: The employer picks one model, and employees have no choice
options.D: The union selects protectors for all employees

questions.explanation: "Employees shall be given the opportunity to select their hearing protectors from a variety of suitable hearing protectors provided by the employer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.95(l)(1) require the employer to do with copies of the noise standard?

options.A: Keep them only in the safety office
options.B: Give them only to supervisors
options.C: Make them available to affected employees or their representatives, and post a copy in the workplace
options.D: Send them only to OSHA

questions.explanation: "The employer shall make available to affected employees or their representatives copies of this standard and shall also post a copy in the workplace."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employer ceases to do business. What does 1910.95(m)(5) require for the records kept under the noise standard?

options.A: Destroy them right away
options.B: Transfer them to the successor employer, who keeps them for the rest of the required period
options.C: Keep only the most recent year's records
options.D: Give each record to the employee's supervisor

questions.explanation: "If the employer ceases to do business, the employer shall transfer to the successor employer all records required to be maintained by this section, and the successor employer shall retain them for the remainder of the period prescribed in paragraph (m)(3) of this section."
